q: The relations between linear quantities and angular quantities for circular motion have been studied in Grade 11.
e: True. The relations between linear quantities and angular quantities for circular motion have been studied in Grade 11. Keep the exact quantity, direction or number named in the statement.

q: All particles of an object rotating around the axis of rotation move in a circular path.
e: True. All particles of an object rotating around the axis of rotation move in a circular path. Every particle of a rigid body shares the same axis and travels on its own circle.

q: Only the particles on the outer edge of an object rotating around the axis of rotation move in a circular path.
e: False. Particles at every radius move in circles about the axis, not just the outer edge. The error is the part about particles outer edge object rotating around.

q: All particles of a rotating body move in a circle lying on a plane that is perpendicular to the axis.
e: True. All particles of a rotating body move in a circle lying on a plane that is perpendicular to the axis. Each particle's circle lies in a plane at right angles to the rotation axis.

q: All particles of a rotating body move in a circle lying on a plane that is parallel to the axis.
e: False. Each circular path lies in a plane perpendicular to the axis. Each particle's circle lies in a plane perpendicular to the axis.

q: The centre of rotation of the circular path of a particle in a rotating body lies on the axis.
e: True. The centre of rotation of the circular path of a particle in a rotating body lies on the axis. The centre of that circle sits on the axis of rotation.

q: The relation between arc length $s$ and angular displacement $	heta$, measured in radian, is $s = r 	heta$.
e: True. The relation between arc length s and angular displacement heta, measured in radian, is s = r heta. Angular displacement θ is the angle the body turns, measured in radians in the s = rθ family of equations.

q: The relation between arc length $s$ and angular displacement $	heta$, measured in degree, is $s = r 	heta$.
e: False. s = rθ needs θ in radians, not degrees. s = rθ is valid only when θ is in radians, not degrees.

q: Since the direction of linear velocity is tangent to the path, the linear velocity is also called tangential velocity.
e: True. Since the direction of linear velocity is tangent to the path, the linear velocity is also called tangential velocity. Linear velocity is tangent to the path, so it is also called tangential velocity.

q: Since the direction of linear velocity is perpendicular to the path, the linear velocity is also called radial velocity.
e: False. Velocity is tangent to the path, so it is tangential velocity, not radial. The error is the part about Since direction linear velocity perpendicular path.

q: If the magnitude of the linear velocity changes, the object will have a tangential acceleration.
e: True. If the magnitude of the linear velocity changes, the object will have a tangential acceleration. Tangential acceleration a_T lies along the tangent and changes the speed along the circle.

q: If the magnitude of the linear velocity changes, the object will have a centripetal acceleration only.
e: False. If speed changes there is also tangential acceleration, not centripetal acceleration alone. The error is the part about magnitude linear velocity changes object centripetal.

q: The direction of tangential acceleration is always tangent to the circular path.
e: True. The direction of tangential acceleration is always tangent to the circular path. Tangential acceleration a_T lies along the tangent and changes the speed along the circle.

q: The direction of tangential acceleration is always perpendicular to the circular path.
e: False. Tangential acceleration a_T is tangent to the path, not perpendicular to it. The perpendicular direction is radial.

q: The tangential acceleration of a rotating object is a measure of how fast the tangential velocity changes.
e: True. The tangential acceleration of a rotating object is a measure of how fast the tangential velocity changes. Tangential acceleration a_T lies along the tangent and changes the speed along the circle.

q: The tangential acceleration of a rotating object is a measure of how fast the angular displacement changes.
e: False. Tangential acceleration measures how fast the linear speed changes, through a_T = rα. The error is the part about tangential acceleration rotating object measure fast.

q: The direction of the angular velocity vector is perpendicular to the plane of rotation.
e: True. The direction of the angular velocity vector is perpendicular to the plane of rotation. Angular velocity ω tells how fast the rotation angle is changing.

q: The direction of the angular velocity vector is parallel to the plane of rotation.
e: False. The angular velocity vector lies along the axis, perpendicular to the plane of rotation. The error is the part about direction angular velocity vector parallel plane.

q: The direction of the angular velocity vector is along the axis of rotation.
e: True. The direction of the angular velocity vector is along the axis of rotation. Angular velocity ω tells how fast the rotation angle is changing.

q: The direction of angular velocity is usually specified by the right-hand rule.
e: True. The direction of angular velocity is usually specified by the right-hand rule. Angular velocity ω tells how fast the rotation angle is changing.

q: The direction of angular velocity is usually specified by the left-hand rule.
e: False. Direction of ω is given by the right-hand rule. Use the right-hand rule: fingers curl with the rotation and the thumb gives ω.

q: To use the right-hand rule, wrap the right hand around the axis of rotation so that the fingers are pointing in the direction of rotation.
e: True. To use the right-hand rule, wrap the right hand around the axis of rotation so that the fingers are pointing in the direction of rotation. The right-hand rule sets the sense of the angular velocity vector along the axis.

q: In the right-hand rule, the thumb points in the direction of the angular velocity vector.
e: True. In the right-hand rule, the thumb points in the direction of the angular velocity vector. Angular velocity ω tells how fast the rotation angle is changing.

q: In the right-hand rule, the fingers point in the direction of the angular velocity vector.
e: False. In the right-hand rule the thumb points along ω; the fingers curl with the rotation. The error is the part about right-hand rule fingers point direction angular.

q: When the angular velocity is increasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the same direction as the angular velocity.
e: True. When the angular velocity is increasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the same direction as the angular velocity. Angular acceleration α is the rate of change of angular velocity ω.

q: When the angular velocity is increasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the opposite direction to the angular velocity.
e: False. When ω is increasing, α points in the same direction as ω. The error is the part about angular velocity increasing acceleration vector points.

q: When the angular velocity is decreasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the opposite to the angular velocity.
e: True. When the angular velocity is decreasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the opposite to the angular velocity. Angular acceleration α is the rate of change of angular velocity ω.

q: When the angular velocity is decreasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the same direction as the angular velocity.
e: False. When ω is decreasing, α is opposite to ω. The error is the part about angular velocity decreasing acceleration vector points.
